City council approves new park

The council voted on Tuesday to approve a new riverside park. Construction begins next spring and is expected to take two years.

The eleven-hectare site along the east bank will include a playground, a community garden, a cycling path linking the old harbour to the market district, and a restored wetland that planners say will reduce flooding in the neighbourhoods downstream.

What residents said

More than four hundred people attended the public consultation in September. Most asked for more shade trees and better lighting; several local schools requested an outdoor classroom, which the final plan now includes near the northern entrance.

“We have waited a long time for green space on this side of the river,” said one resident who has lived in the area for thirty years. “This changes how the whole neighbourhood feels.”

Cost and timeline

The project is funded through a combination of municipal bonds and a regional climate grant. The first phase, covering the wetland and the cycling path, is scheduled to open to the public in the summer after next.
